daily.title: Who-to-ask finder that reads your git history
daily.pitch: Point it at a file or folder and it tells you who knows that code best, based on recent, meaningful commits.
daily.problem: New developers waste days asking the wrong people, and nobody notices when only one person understands a critical module.
daily.whoPays: Developers for free; teams pay for bus-factor reports.
daily.pricing: Free and open source; $8 per seat per month for team reports.
daily.stack: Go with go-git, or Rust with git2
mvp: Rank people per file by recent commits and lines owned
daily.firstUsers: Run it on 20 popular open-source repos and publish the 'bus factor' results as a blog post.

daily.title: A command journal that remembers what you ran in each project
daily.pitch: Every command you run is saved per project with its exit code and an optional note, so 'how did I fix this last time?' has an answer.
daily.problem: Shell history is one giant list with no context, and the fix you found last month is gone.
daily.whoPays: Developers; teams pay to share runbooks.
daily.pricing: Free; $4 per month for encrypted sync across machines.
daily.stack: Rust, hooking into bash, zsh and fish
mvp: Record commands with folder, exit code and time
Attach a note to any command
daily.firstUsers: Post a demo on r/commandline built around the 'how did I fix this last time?' story.

daily.title: One command to start deep work
daily.pitch: Run 'focus 90' and it mutes notifications, sets your Slack status, blocks distracting sites and logs the session.
daily.problem: Starting focused work takes five small steps, so most people never do them.
daily.whoPays: Developers and writers; teams pay for team focus stats.
daily.pricing: Free; $3 per month for stats and integrations.
daily.stack: Go, with the Slack and calendar APIs
mvp: Timer with do-not-disturb on macOS, Windows and Linux
daily.firstUsers: Share your own weekly focus stats on X and invite others to post theirs.

daily.title: Blast-radius map: what breaks if you change this function
daily.pitch: Point it at a function and it lists every caller, test and endpoint that depends on it, before you touch anything.
daily.problem: Developers change 'small' functions and break things three modules away because the dependencies aren't visible.
daily.whoPays: Teams with large or old codebases.
daily.pricing: Free for public repos; $15 per seat per month for private ones.
mvp: Parse one language really well first
Call graph for a chosen function
Map to the tests that cover it
Pull-request comment with the blast radius
daily.firstUsers: Offer free reports to maintainers of three big open-source projects and publish the results.

daily.title: README doctor: checks that your setup instructions actually work
daily.pitch: It reads your README, runs the install steps in a clean container, and tells you exactly which step fails.
daily.problem: Most READMEs break within months, and newcomers give up at step three.
daily.whoPays: Open-source maintainers for free; companies for internal repos.
daily.pricing: Free for open source; $10 per month per private repo.
daily.stack: Python with Docker, as a CLI and a GitHub Action
mvp: Extract the shell blocks from the README
Run them in a fresh container
Report the first failing step with logs
A 'README verified' badge with the date
daily.firstUsers: Run it on 50 popular repos and open friendly issues for the ones that fail.

daily.title: Print your to-do list on a cheap receipt printer
daily.pitch: Send tasks, tickets or today's calendar to a small thermal printer: one paper slip per task, to tear off and crumple when done.
daily.problem: Digital to-do lists are easy to ignore; a physical slip on your desk is not.
daily.whoPays: Makers and productivity fans; sell printer bundles.
daily.pricing: Free and open source; printer bundles sold with a margin.
mvp: Print a task as a slip with a checkbox
Import from GitHub issues or a text file
Templates for tickets and shopping lists
daily.firstUsers: Post a satisfying video of tearing off finished tasks; this one sells itself on video.

daily.title: Lecture recordings to searchable notes, from the terminal
daily.pitch: Give it a lecture recording and the slides; get timestamped notes split by slide, plus a list of moments that sound like exam hints.
daily.problem: Students record lectures and never rewatch two hours of audio to find the one explanation they need.
daily.whoPays: Students for free; tutors and course creators pay.
daily.pricing: Free with local models; $5 per month for fast cloud processing.
daily.firstUsers: Process one full course for your batch before exams and share the notes.

daily.title: Port bouncer: find out what's on port 3000 and kick it off
daily.pitch: Shows every process listening on a port with its project folder and start time, and stops it with one key.
daily.problem: 'Address already in use' costs developers minutes every day hunting for zombie dev servers.
daily.pricing: Free and open source, funded by sponsors.
daily.stack: Rust, a single binary for every OS
mvp: List listening ports with process and folder
Identical on macOS, Linux and Windows
daily.firstUsers: Answer the top Stack Overflow questions about 'address already in use' with a link where it genuinely helps.

daily.title: Explain your SQL query's cost in plain English before you run it
daily.pitch: Give it a query and it runs EXPLAIN, then says in plain words why it will be slow and which index would fix it.
daily.problem: Developers ship queries that scan millions of rows because EXPLAIN output is unreadable.
daily.whoPays: Backend developers; teams pay for CI checks on migrations.
daily.pricing: Free; $12 per month for the CI check.
daily.stack: Go with Postgres and MySQL drivers
mvp: Run EXPLAIN safely against a read replica
daily.firstUsers: Write a blog post fixing a slow query step by step with the tool.

daily.title: Scrub API keys you accidentally pasted into your shell history
daily.pitch: Scans your shell history and dotfiles for tokens and passwords, shows what it found, and removes them safely.
daily.problem: Developers paste secrets into commands all the time, and they sit in plain-text history files for years.
daily.pricing: Free; $5 per developer per month for company scans.
daily.stack: Go, with patterns for common token formats
mvp: Optional hook that warns before saving
daily.firstUsers: Post the scary stat from scanning your own history, values masked, on Hacker News.

daily.title: Offline docs for your exact dependency versions
daily.pitch: Downloads the documentation for every library at the versions in your lockfile, so you can search it on a plane.
daily.problem: Online docs show the latest version, not the one you use, and they're useless on bad internet.
daily.whoPays: Developers who travel or have poor internet; teams with offline machines.
daily.stack: Rust with a local full-text index
mvp: Fetch docs for the exact versions
Open results in the terminal or browser
daily.firstUsers: Share it in digital-nomad and developer communities in places with patchy internet.

daily.title: A terminal pet that grows with your commit streak
daily.pitch: A tiny creature lives in your prompt; it thrives when you commit daily and gets dramatic when you don't.
daily.problem: Coding habits fade fast, and streak apps live somewhere you don't look while coding.
daily.whoPays: Developers for cosmetics; teams for a shared pet.
daily.stack: Go, printing a tiny status in the prompt
mvp: Pet status in the shell prompt
Mood based on the commit streak
daily.firstUsers: Post the pet's dramatic 'you haven't committed in 3 days' screen on r/ProgrammerHumor.

daily.title: Flaky test hunter
daily.pitch: Runs your test suite many times, ranks tests by how often they fail at random, and shows what they have in common.
daily.problem: Flaky tests teach teams to ignore red builds, which is how real bugs slip through.
daily.pricing: Free locally; $20 per month for the CI dashboard.
daily.stack: Python, with adapters for pytest and Jest
mvp: Run tests many times in parallel
A report ready for a pull request
daily.firstUsers: Ask on dev.to who has the worst flaky test, then hunt it down in a follow-up post.

daily.title: Turn your repo's history into a 30-second time-lapse video
daily.pitch: Renders your project's growth as a video, with files appearing, contributors joining and milestones popping up, ready for a launch post.
daily.problem: Makers want to show the journey behind a launch, but screenshots of commit graphs are boring.
daily.pricing: Free with a watermark; $9 per video without.
mvp: Animated file tree and contributor avatars
Export MP4 in square and vertical sizes
daily.firstUsers: Make time-lapses for five well-known open-source projects and post them.
